speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Transport in light of the recent incident of an SBS bus driver being abused (a) what more can the Ministry do to protect our bus captains and transport service staff; (b) how can high-risk passenger management procedures be enhanced; (c) whether a public awareness campaign directed at passengers to encourage respect for bus drivers and to outline expected behaviours while travelling on public transport can be explored; and (d) whether a code of conduct for passengers can be developed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: They are in charge of the bus and ensure the safety of commuters throughout their journeys.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In today's context, this includes ensuring commuters wear masks, so that public transport does not become a transmission setting.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: I think people all know that, and it is not a matter of writing down a code of conduct.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: What we need is to take a clear stand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The large majority of commuters treat our public transport workers and other commuters with courtesy and respect.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Commuters too can play a part when such incidents happen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: For the recent case where a bus captain was attacked by a commuter who refused to wear his mask properly, three good Samaritans helped to restrain the assailant before the Police arrived.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: I met two of them, Mr Clement Tan and Mr Muhammad Mu’tasim.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Mr Melvin Yong was there too at the recent event; he was representing the National Transport Workers' Union.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Mr Tan was a commando during his National Service and Mr Mu’tasim served his National Service as a Police officer.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: We applaud them for their courage to step forward and do the right thing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The best way to protect our bus captains and recognise their contributions is to have the right societal culture, one that is based on respect for our frontline workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Let us continue to support our public transport workers, so that they can work in a safe environment and provide an essential service to keep Singapore going.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With regard to his zero-tolerance approach to the issue, I am reassured that LTA and MOT will take this zero-tolerance approach very strongly against commuters who get offensive against the bus captains.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: They also ran a public awareness campaign from June to December 2018.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, my question is whether LTA or MOT will be willing to explore such a review and encourage best practices between our multiple bus operators?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Because, after all, a bus driver who feels safe means all passengers are safe.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The zero-tolerance approach that we take is towards abusive behaviours by a small number of commuters.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Saktiandi has touched on a very important point, which is that this requires the collective effort of Government, operators, unions and I will add commuters too.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: All of us as stakeholders in this public transport system can play our role.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: For the on-going review that we are conducting with the operators and the unions, I would welcome further suggestions on what are some of the specific measures we can put in place to offer greater protection to our frontline workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I declare myself as the Executive Secretary of the National Transport Workers' Union.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We would also take feedback from our bus captains because they are the ones who will be using this.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: When this safeguard is in place, they will be the ones who are going to use it daily.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think an important consideration when we ask the bus captains for their feedback, will be to ensure that the installation of these protective shields will not interfere with the safety when they are driving the buses.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, we will also have to look at that because, ultimately, this is for both the protection and safety of the bus captains and also for the safety of commuters.
